questions.question_text: Choose the correct expression for the band gap (Eg) of materials from the following?
questions.answer: The band gap is defined as the energy difference between the bottom of the conduction band (Ec) and the top of the valence band (Ev).

questions.question_text: The range of wave number (k) for the first Brillouin zone is __________.
questions.answer: For a one-dimensional lattice with lattice constant 'a', the first Brillouin zone is defined in the range [-π/a, π/a].

questions.question_text: In a metal, the electron always move __________ in the absence of electric field.
options: In the direction of electric field
questions.answer: Without an external field, electrons move randomly due to thermal energy, resulting in zero net current.

questions.question_text: Phonon is a quantum of __________
questions.answer: A phonon is the quantized unit of collective vibrational motion (lattice vibrations) in a crystal.

questions.question_text: In LED, what is the shape of domes made from plastics used to minimize the losses caused by bulk absorption thereby increasing the external efficiency?
questions.answer: Hemispherical domes reduce total internal reflection at the plastic-air interface, allowing more light to escape.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: Auger generation/recombination is also known as __________
questions.answer: Auger recombination is a non-radiative process involving three particles (e.g., two electrons and one hole).
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: If "n" and "p" denotes the number of electrons in the conduction and holes in the valence band, for an intrinsic semiconductor __________
questions.answer: In intrinsic semiconductors, carriers are created only by thermal excitation of electrons from valence to conduction band, so the number of electrons must equal the number of holes.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: To obtain an p-type semiconductor, an intrinsic semiconductor is doped with which of the below?
questions.answer: Boron is a trivalent impurity (Group III) which creates holes in Silicon/Germanium, forming p-type material.
questions.chapter: Unit 2- Carrier Transport Mechanism in Semiconductors

questions.question_text: If the number of upward transition per seconds exceeds the number of downward transition, __________ is achieved
questions.answer: If upward transitions (absorption) exceed downward transitions (emission), there is net absorption, i.e. optical loss. Optical gain needs downward transitions to exceed upward ones (population inversion).

questions.question_text: Which of the below is an inter band transition?
questions.answer: Interband transitions occur between the valence band and the conduction band.

questions.question_text: The generation of electron-hole pairs by the incidence of light followed by their radiative recombination is known as
questions.answer: Photoluminescence is the emission of light from a material after the absorption of photons.

questions.question_text: The Fermi's golden rule helps to identify the __________
questions.answer: Fermi's Golden Rule is used to calculate the transition probability (rate) between quantum states.

questions.question_text: If the Hall voltage is positive in, the sample is a __________.
questions.answer: A positive Hall voltage indicates that the majority charge carriers are holes, which is the case for p-type semiconductors.

questions.question_text: If the measured voltage is positive in hot point probe method, the sample is a __________.
questions.answer: In the hot probe method the hot probe is taken as the positive lead. In an n-type sample, electrons diffuse from the hot probe to the cold probe, leaving the hot probe positive, so a positive reading indicates n-type (a negative reading indicates p-type).

questions.question_text: The resistance of a material is inversely proportional to the __________.
questions.answer: Resistance R = ρL/A, meaning R is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area A.

questions.question_text: In four probe method, the outer two contacts are connected to __________.
questions.answer: In a linear four-point probe, current is passed through the outer probes and voltage is measured across the inner probes.

questions.question_text: The notation for arm chair carbon nanotube can be written as __________.
questions.answer: Armchair carbon nanotubes are characterized by chiral indices (n, n).

questions.question_text: High resolution Transmission electron microscopy helps us to see the __________ of the sample.
questions.answer: HRTEM has high enough resolution to image individual atoms and crystal planes.

questions.question_text: In a 1D material, the density of states is __________.
questions.answer: For a one-dimensional system (quantum wire), the Density of States (DOS) follows an E⁻¹/² dependency.

questions.question_text: The material size is reduced in one direction and the electron can move freely only in two directions in __________.
questions.answer: A quantum well or thin sheet is confined in one dimension, allowing free motion in the remaining two dimensions.
